title: inbox POST skips spec 18.1.1 field types
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py

Correctness: render_post validates body/text as str, canned as catalog uint, and id as u64. It then persists the rest of the decoded map unchanged.

Spec 18.1.1 types: to tstr (IPv6 or ff02::1), ts uint, ack bool, priority uint 0..2, reply_to uint, ttl uint. Firmware POST /msg/sent rejects non-IPv6 to and non-bool ack (coap_msg.c:431-450).

Confirmed: POST {body, ack:'yes', priority:9, read:True} is 2.01 Created; those values are stored; unread_count() is 0 because read is truthy. Unknown keys are echoed on GET /msg/inbox.

unread_count (line 163) treats any truthy read as read, so a client-controlled extra key poisons spec 18.1.2 unread.
acceptance_criteria: If present, to is a string, ack is bool, priority is 0/1/2, and ts/ttl/reply_to are u64; otherwise 4.00 and no mutation. Client-supplied read (and other non-spec keys) are not stored. unread_count only counts messages not marked read by a local/authorized path.
